Time Clauses: As soon as, when and while

You use time clauses in complex sentences. These kinds of sentences have an dependent clause and an independent clause which are joined by a connector that refers to a specific point or period of time.
Common time markers that act as connectors are: as soon as, when and while.
As soon as refers to something that happens immediately.
For example:
As soon as I had my daughter, everything changed.
When refers to a period of our lives.
For example:
When I was a child, social media didn't exist.
While refers to a period of time.
For example:
While my daughter was growing, I found that she was becoming more and more unmotivated

images.text: Denise: I'm thrilled to see that so many of you have come out tonight. We're gathered here to celebrate the official release of Ms. Marisa Mitchell's book! It has been a tremendous honour for BFP to work with her. And now, without further ado, put your hands together and give a warm welcome to the star of the night.

Marisa: Oh Denise, thank you so very much for those kind words. The honor was all mine. You run a tight ship. And to all of you, thank you for taking the time to come support me. I've been overwhelmed by the support I have received. Ever since I was in junior high, I knew I wanted to write a book, to become an author. I was unsure what I would write about but I'd have a great idea one day, and now here we are, 25 years later. It wasn't until I became a mother, that this idea would come to life. As soon as I had my daughter, everything changed. The way I looked at the world had changed. When I was a child, social media didn't exist. We would spend hours upon hours playing outside.

But as many of you know, that isn't the case now. Children are glued to their screens. While my daughter was growing, I found that she was becoming more and more unmotivated. I was unsettled by the fact that she knew how to use all these devices.  She could find videos on the internet, she wanted her own flash drive and would spend hours on her games console with a controller or joystick stuck to her hand. While technology continues to advance, us parents, we are often perplexed and overwhelmed by all of it . What new devices will pop up? How long will  it before technology takes over our children's lives? Or until people are walking around wearing an optical head-mounted display? It was questions like this, that lead to the premise behind Winnie's World.

But as many of you know, that isn't the case now. Children are glued to their screens. While my daughter was growing up, I found she was becoming more and more unmotivated. I was unsettled by the fact that she knew how to use all these different devices.
